name: Clear floors and walkways
description: Keep walkways open. Loose rugs, cords, and clutter are easy to trip on.
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.

name: Bright, even lighting
description: Use bright light in halls, stairs, and bathrooms, including at night.
intendedUse: Make walking paths easier to see
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.

name: Bathroom steadiness
description: A shower seat, grab bars, and a non-slip surface are common supports. Placement and install matter.
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.

name: Eating and kitchen aids overview
description: Built-up or weighted utensils, and items kept within easy reach, can make meals simpler when hands shake or feel stiff.
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Assistive Tech Devices page, paraphrased.

name: Dressing aids overview
description: Button hooks, sock aids, and simpler clothing can reduce fine-motor strain while dressing.
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Assistive Tech Devices page, paraphrased.

name: Walking aids overview
description: Canes and walkers are options to discuss with a physical therapist. Fit and training matter more than the brand.
intendedUse: Walking support to discuss with a therapist
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Assistive Tech Devices page, paraphrased.

name: Reach and bending overview
description: Keeping everyday items at arm level, and using a reacher, can cut down on stretching and rushing.
safetyNotes: General information only. A therapist can look at the specific home and the person.
source: Parkinson's Foundation Home Safety page, paraphrased.
